agent_summary:
Target juice.lab.test answers only on HTTP (nginx/1.30.5 reverse proxy; HTTPS/443 refused). It is OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0 on Node.js + Express ^4.22.1 serving an Angular SPA (hash routing), with a REST/JSON API (/api/*, /rest/*), a static /ftp file server (serve-index), an unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics exporter, socket.io/engine.io realtime, a gemma LLM chatbot, Google OAuth and a Sequelize/SQLite backend. All 10 WSTG-INFO items were performed with read-only requests (plus authenticated calls as test accounts info1/info2/conf1); 120 requests made, meeting the depth floor.

Reachable surface confirmed: /, robots.txt (→/ftp), /.well-known/security.txt + /.well-known/csaf/*, /metrics, /rest/admin/application-version and application-configuration, many /api models and /rest endpoints, SPA bundles (main.js, polyfills, scripts, and hashed lazy modules), /video, /encryptionkeys, /support/logs, /ftp. The server uses an SPA catch-all (unknown paths return 200 index.html, explaining empty known_paths); some /rest paths 404 at nginx. No source maps, /.git, or /.env exposed.

Key findings recorded as leads for a validator:
- HIGH: /rest/memories (unauth) leaks full user records incl. password hashes/roles/tokens; /ftp/incident-support.kdbx (KeePass DB) downloads directly; null-byte allowlist bypass (%2500.md) retrieves /ftp/package.json.bak (with a JWT secret) and coupons_2013.md.bak.
- MEDIUM: /api/Users/:id BOLA (info1 read user ids 1–3); /rest/basket/:id IDOR (identical body to two accounts); /rest/user/authentication-details returns all users to any logged-in user; directory listings at /ftp, /encryptionkeys (premium.key, jwt.pub downloadable), /support/logs; wallet mnemonic leaked in /api/Feedbacks.
- LOW/INFO: full app config disclosure, wildcard CORS (ACAO:* everywhere; socket.io set to localhost:4200), weak CSP (unsafe-eval) on /profile, verbose Node stack traces on errors, unauthenticated /metrics.

Nothing was left open. Writes were allowed but not needed (all tests were read-only). State-changing probes of action-named endpoints (password/erasure/redirect targets) were avoided per policy; the IDOR/BOLA leads should be validated by the access-control lane, and the exposed secret files (kdbx, package.json.bak JWT, encryption keys) warrant follow-up.

leads.title: [agent] /api/Users/:id BOLA allows enumeration of the full user table

detail.text: As test account info1, GET /api/Users/1, /api/Users/2 and /api/Users/3 each return HTTP 200 with a distinct user record (each containing an email address), confirming sequential-id enumeration of other users. The collection /api/Users is 401 but the per-id route has no ownership/role check.

leads.title: [agent] /rest/user/authentication-details returns all users' details to any logged-in user

detail.text: GET /rest/user/authentication-details as ordinary test account info1 returns a 14.5KB response containing 38 distinct user email addresses (and associated records), i.e. the whole user table rather than just the caller's own data — broken access control / information disclosure.

leads.title: [agent] Allowlist bypass via null byte exposes backup file /ftp/package.json.bak

detail.text: GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (poison null byte) returns HTTP 200 with the full 4263-byte package.json.bak (octet-stream), bypassing the ".md and .pdf only" fileServer allowlist that returns 403 for the plain name. The stored response contains a jsonwebtoken value and an email address (flagged by the gateway redactor). Directory-traversal/null-byte file disclosure of a backup file with secrets.

leads.title: [agent] Any authenticated user can read arbitrary user records via /api/Users/:id

detail.text: GET /api/Users/1 as ordinary test account info1 returns HTTP 200 with a single user object (301 bytes, includes an email address) for user id 1, while GET /api/Users (collection) is 401. The per-id endpoint lacks an ownership check, allowing enumeration of other users' records (BOLA/IDOR, information disclosure). By contrast /rest/order-history/orders correctly returns 403 for non-admins.

leads.title: [agent] Crypto wallet mnemonic/seed phrase exposed in public /api/Feedbacks data

detail.text: GET /api/Feedbacks (unauthenticated) returns feedback id 4 (UserId 21) whose comment contains a 12-word BIP39-style mnemonic: "purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch" referencing a wallet at /juicy-nft. Sensitive secret disclosed in publicly readable data.

leads.title: [agent] Directory listing and sensitive backup files exposed at /ftp

detail.text: GET /ftp returns a directory listing of 11 entries including incident-support.kdbx (KeePass DB), package.json.bak, package-lock.json.bak, coupons_2013.md.bak, announcement_encrypted.md, encrypt.pyc, suspicious_errors.yml, acquisitions.md, eastere.gg, legal.md and a quarantine folder. robots.txt points to /ftp. These files may contain credentials/coupons/source and should be reviewed (file-download access may be filtered by extension in Juice Shop).

GET /encryptionkeys returns HTTP 200 with a browsable HTML directory listing (7954 bytes, serve-index). This folder in Juice Shop holds encryption key material; exposing it as a listing allows discovery/download of key files.

leads.title: [agent] Directory listing of server logs exposed at /support/logs

detail.text: GET /support/logs returns HTTP 200 with a browsable HTML directory listing (8923 bytes, serve-index) of server log files. Access logs frequently contain tokens, session ids or other sensitive data in request URLs; exposing them anonymously is an information-disclosure risk.

GET /rest/admin/application-configuration (no auth) returns the entire server config: Google OAuth clientId, authorizedRedirects, chatbot LLM model (gemma4:e4b), privacy contact email, internal baseUrl http://localhost:3000, challenge settings, etc. Information disclosure of internal deployment details.

leads.title: [agent] Full user records (password hashes, tokens, roles) leaked via /rest/memories

detail.text: GET /rest/memories with no authentication returns photo-wall entries each embedding the complete User object: password hash, email, role (e.g. user id 4 username "bkimminich" role "admin"), deluxeToken and totpSecret. Sensitive user/credential data exposed to anonymous users.

leads.title: [agent] IDOR on /rest/basket/:id confirmed across two accounts

detail.text: GET /rest/basket/1 returns an identical body (same ETag W/"51e-PnJ4RtdB/iietnrwfRS0ftkuz2U") to two distinct freshly-registered accounts (info1 and info2). Neither owns basket id 1, yet both receive the same 1310-byte basket, confirming the endpoint returns another user's basket without an ownership check.

GET /ftp/incident-support.kdbx returns HTTP 200, Content-Type application/octet-stream, 3246 bytes (the full file from the /ftp listing) with no authentication. Unlike /ftp/package.json.bak (403 "Only .md and .pdf files are allowed"), the .kdbx is served directly, exposing a KeePass password database that could be cracked offline.

leads.title: [agent] Possible IDOR: /rest/basket/1 returns data to an unrelated account

detail.text: GET /rest/basket/1 as freshly-registered test account info1 returns HTTP 200 with a 1310-byte JSON basket. Since info1 is a new account (its own basket id would differ), reading basket id 1 suggests missing ownership enforcement on /rest/basket/:id (BOLA). Recommend the access-control lane confirm info1's own basket id vs the returned data.

GET /metrics returns full Prometheus metrics with no authentication: process memory/CPU, open FDs, event-loop lag, HTTP status-code counts, LLM token counters, and startup task timings. Discloses internal runtime details and request volume. Note this endpoint (and only this one) returned without the CORS/x-frame security headers present elsewhere.

leads.title: [agent] Verbose error stack traces disclose server file paths and framework versions

detail.text: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns HTTP 403 with a full Node/Express stack trace in the body: absolute paths (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:68, /juice-shop/node_modules/express/lib/router/...), "OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.22.1)". Error handling leaks internal structure and dependency versions.

leads.title: [agent] Wildcard CORS (ACAO:*) on all responses and weak CSP (unsafe-eval) on /profile

detail.text: Every response includes Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (including authenticated REST/API JSON like /api/Cards, /rest/wallet/balance), and OPTIONS /rest/user/login confirms wildcard CORS with all methods allowed. The server-rendered /profile page sets Content-Security-Policy "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval'", which permits eval-based script execution.
